### [Introducing GPT-6 Astra for developers](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/5/introducing-gpt-6-astra-for-developers/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-05

OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Astra for developers, featuring improved prompt understanding, higher attention to detail, and specialized capabilities in generating 3D models.

- Demonstrates improved prompt comprehension and greater attention to detail across general tasks.
- Capable of generating complex, sophisticated outputs, with specific strengths in 3D model creation.
- Successfully renders complex 3D scenes including gardens, shipyards, animals, cityscapes, and Dyson spheres.

**Why it matters:** Developers gain access to an upgraded model capable of generating significantly more sophisticated outputs and complex 3D renderings.

### [The Pelican comparison grid for Astra is pretty interesting](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/4/astra-pelicans/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-04

A comparative evaluation of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra against GPT-5.6 models on SVG generation tasks demonstrates significantly improved visual fidelity and lower token consumption despite higher per-token pricing.

- GPT-6 Astra costs $10/M input and $50/M output tokens compared to GPT-5.6 Sol at $5/M input and $30/M output tokens.
- Astra generates higher-quality SVGs at its lowest reasoning setting ('low', costing $0.0955) than any GPT-5.6 Sol reasoning level.
- Astra and Luna both used 16 input tokens for the prompt, compared to 26 input tokens used by Sol and Terra.
- Astra does not support a 'reasoning=none' setting, and levels below 'max' fail to reliably render pelican legs on both sides of the bicycle frame.

**Why it matters:** Astra's reduced token usage offsets its higher base pricing, making it more cost-effective than GPT-5.6 for complex generative SVG tasks.
